**Finding submitted: deviation (§ 14.10 Assignment, p0188).**

**What the document says.** § 14.10 restricts only us: Customer may not assign without IBM's consent (not unreasonably withheld), with a carve-out permitting assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition, and we remain liable post-assignment. IBM's own assignment right is not addressed at all — and § 14.18 affirmatively contemplates "assignees of IBM Corp." A full-text search confirms there is **no** change-of-control provision anywhere, so IBM has no termination or re-pricing trigger on our change of control (no walk-away issue).

**Why it fails the fallback.** The fallback requires a *mutual* right to assign to successors with a not-unreasonably-withheld consent standard for other assignments. Here IBM is entirely unrestricted — no consent gate and no bar on assigning to one of our competitors — so the mutuality element of the fallback is absent on a material term. (Our side's M&A carve-out is adequate; the missing affiliate carve-out alone would have been a rationale note, not a deviation.)

**Redline (validated ok:true).** One targeted replacement in p0188 that (i) adds an affiliate and sale-of-substantially-all-assets carve-out for our consent-free assignments, and (ii) subjects IBM's assignment to our prior written consent, not unreasonably withheld, and never to a Customer competitor. This reaches the preferred position; the reciprocal-consent sentence alone is a sensible fallback if IBM pushes back on the affiliate carve-out.
